chunks: Aḥmad, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Jabbār, from Abū ʿAbdillāh al-Barqī, from Faḍālah ibn Ayyūb, from Sulaymān ibn Khālid, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
No scholar dies until Allah, Mighty and Majestic, informs him to whom he should make his bequest.

key_terms.عَالِمٌ: a scholar; here, in context, the divinely guided Imam عليه السلام
key_terms.عَزَّ وَجَلَّ: Mighty and Majestic; an honorific description of Allah
key_terms.يُعْلِمَهُ: He informs him; Allah gives him knowledge of the matter
key_terms.يُوصِي: he makes a bequest or appoints in trust

ai.seo_question: How does an Imam عليه السلام know whom to appoint before his passing?
ai.summary: This hadith states that a divinely guided scholar is not taken in death until Allah, Mighty and Majestic, makes known to him the one to whom he must entrust his bequest. In the chapter context, it signifies the continuity of divine authority and the orderly designation of the succeeding Imam عليه السلام.

en.hubeali:
Ahmad, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Abu Abdullah Al Barqy, from Fazalat Bin Ayoub, from Suleyman Bin Khalid, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘A scholar (Imam<sup>asws</sup>) does not pass away until Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Lets him<sup>asws</sup> know to whom he<sup>asws</sup> should be bequeathing to’.
en.sarwar: 7. Ahmad has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Jabbar from abu ‘Abdallah al-Barqi from Fudalah ibn Ayyub from Sulayman ibn Khalid from abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) who has said the following.
“No scholar (Imam) has ever died before Allah, the Most Holy, the Most High, would grant him the knowledge of to who must he deliver his will.”
